proof.text: Proof: the equality of geometric points gives the functor from pointed etale neighbourhoods of S to those of T by base change. Its maps to the two colimits induce the morphism from strictHenselizationScheme t to strictHenselizationScheme s over g. Transport through eA and eB, then use the fully faithful contravariant Spec functor to obtain the ring homomorphism. On closed points this sends the selected geometric point to the selected geometric point; the corresponding map of local rings is local. The colimit cone compatibility gives the structural equality.

theorem Etale.exists_compatibleStrictHenselizationCoreCompletion
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} {g : T ⟶ S}
    {Ω A B : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [HenselianLocalRing A] [HenselianLocalRing B]
    [IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)]
    [IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)]
    {s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S} {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T}
    (hst : s = t ≫ g)
    (eA : Spec (.of A) ≅ strictHenselizationScheme s)
    (eB : Spec (.of B) ≅ strictHenselizationScheme t) :
    ∃ (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : IsLocalHom φ),
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ≫ eA.hom ≫
          strictHenselizationStructuralMap s =
        eB.hom ≫ strictHenselizationStructuralMap t ≫ g

statement: Given geometric points s and t over the same algebraically closed field with s = t composed with g, and affine strictly henselian presentations eA and eB of their strict henselization schemes, there exists a local ring map A to B whose spectrum map commutes with the structural maps over g.
